findings.text: Address space error recording ignores success and otherwise records the failure in three places: the mapping writeback error sequence, the host superblock error sequence when a host exists, and a legacy flag distinguishing no-space from generic IO failure.

Address space exposes flag accessors for unevictable set clear and test with null tolerance, exiting set and test, no-writeback-tags set with inverted use test, release-always test set clear, stable-writes test set clear, inaccessible set and test, and writeback-may-deadlock-on-reclaim set and test.
Address space carries an allocation mask with a getter returning the stored mask, a constraint helper intersecting it with a caller mask, and a setter assigning a new mask.

Pagecache folio size policy provides a global maximum supported size, per-mapping min and max order configuration with clamping, conveniences for large folios and min-only update, getters for max and min order and derived min page and byte counts and max byte size, plus index alignment down to min folio granularity and predicates for large and PMD-sized support.

Folio to owner helpers return no mapping for swapcache entries versus the cached mapping otherwise, and return the host inode from the folio mapping. Private data helpers attach with an extra reference and flag, replace returning the old pointer without reference change, and detach returning data or null while clearing state and dropping the reference, with page wrappers converting to folio first.

Filemap allocation and lookup helpers allocate folios of given order and policy, allocate single pages, derive readahead mask from mapping mask with no-retry and no-warn additions, and wrap a central get routine with flag presets for plain get, grab with lock accessed and create, find with optional flags, find-locked, find-or-create, nonblocking no-filesystem grab, write-begin with order derived from length and dontcache propagation, and read-through cache page and folio entry points.

Folio and page position arithmetic derives next index and next byte position, file page at an index within a folio, containment of an index, folio start byte position, page byte offset including intra-folio displacement, page index from folio plus intra-folio slot, directory page count from inode size rounded up, blocks per folio from folio size shifted by inode block bits, and linear anonymous offsets from VMA delta plus start offset.

Folio locking and state helpers offer nonblocking trylock, blocking lock, killable lock returning status, fault-aware lock-or-retry returning a fault code, waits for the locked bit with plain and killable forms, conditional dirty cancellation only when dirty, range writeback need testing via page count plus dirty and writeback tags plus range scan, and a mkwrite truncate check classifying a folio as wholly inside, wholly past, or straddling end of file.

Readahead control provides synchronous and asynchronous kickoff built from file, state, mapping and start index, single-folio iteration returning each locked resident folio while releasing the caller reference, and batched page collection bounded by caller array size, plus read-only accessors for byte position, total length, start index, page count and last batch length.
Marking a mapping inaccessible also marks it unevictable, and compaction migrate isolation relies on that coupling to reduce page locking.

Folio order range programming is a no-op without transparent huge page support, clamps both bounds to the global pagecache maximum, raises max up to min when inverted, and stores the pair in dedicated flag subfields; without that support all max and min getters report zero.

Minimum folio extent is a power of two number of pages derived from min order, with byte count by page shift, maximum size by page size shifted by max order, alignment rounding an index down by min page count, large support meaning max order above zero, and PMD support meaning the configured interval includes PMD order except in the disabled build which always reports false.

Get flag carries the requested lookup order in its top six bits, extracted by shift; order zero encodes as no flags while nonzero orders shift into that field, and size to order conversion returns zero up to page size and otherwise the binary logarithm excess over page shift.

Readahead cursor invariants require pending batch count never to exceed remaining pages, each step first consumes the previous batch from remaining count and advances the index, iteration ends with zero batch and null when nothing remains, and the batch walk covers exactly the remaining interval starting at the current index.

Private data lifecycle holds one extra folio reference while attached: attach acquires and marks, change swaps pointers preserving the hold, detach clears flag and pointer and releases exactly once and yields null when no private state was present.
Page wake matching requires identical folio pointers to record a page match, and then requires identical bit numbers to report a full wake match.

A byte range needs writeback only when the mapping holds pages and at least one of dirty or writeback tags is set and the range scan finds writeback state; empty mappings or untagged mappings short-circuit to false.

Folio mutual exclusion uses an atomic test-and-set of the locked bit for trylock; blocking, killable and fault-aware forms first attempt trylock and otherwise sleep in slow paths, with blocking paths annotated as sleeping and page wrappers operating on the enclosing folio.

Waiting on a locked folio first tests the locked state and sleeps on the locked bit only when set, with a killable variant propagating interruption status and returning success immediately when already unlocked.

Batched readahead collection walks the page tree under RCU read protection and expects every visited resident folio to already be locked, while single-folio stepping likewise requires the loaded folio to be locked.

Readahead control groups a file pointer, mapping pointer and readahead state pointer with a private cursor of start index, remaining pages and last batch size plus drop-behind and workingset flags and saved task flags; only the documented accessors should read the private cursor, and a helper macro initializes the public pointers and start index.
Page wait key holds a folio pointer, bit number and match output flag, while the queue entry holds a folio pointer, bit number and embedded wait queue node.

Get flags form a bitwise unsigned type with distinct low bits for accessed, lock, create, write, no-filesystem, no-wait, for-mmap, stable and dontcache semantics, plus a combined write-begin preset of lock plus write plus create plus stable.

Readahead consumption moves from armed with remaining pages, to loading the resident locked folio at the cursor, to accounting its page span as the current batch, to advancing past that batch on the next call, terminating to empty with null once remaining count reaches zero.

Folio private state moves from unmarked with null data, to marked with caller data and held reference on attach, remaining marked across pointer replacement, then back to unmarked with null data and released reference on detach.

Synchronous readahead entry takes mapping, readahead state, file, start index and request length and forwards a constructed control to the synchronous engine; asynchronous entry derives its start from a given folio and forwards folio plus request length to the asynchronous engine.

Write-begin lookup builds write-begin flags plus length-derived order and optional dontcache from the IO control, then looks up or creates a locked stable folio at the index using the mapping allocation mask.
Large folio and PMD support queries are only meaningful for pagecache mappings and warn when given an anonymous mapping marker; anonymous mappings are called out as always supporting large folios.

Resolving an inode through a folio mapping assumes the mapping pointer is valid, so callers must exclude unmapped or swapcache folios first; the flush helper does this by returning null for swapcache.

Containment testing warns when applied to swapcache folios, and readahead stepping enforces locked residency and cursor consistency with bug checks on unlocked folios and on batch counts larger than remaining pages.
Linear anonymous index computation warns when the area is not a copy-on-write mapping and cross-checks semi-anonymous private zero mappings against the linear file index.

Preferred pagecache order has two build alternatives, one following the PMD huge page order and one fixed at eight; the tree order bound derives from twice the chunk shift minus one, and the effective pagecache maximum is the lesser of that bound and the preferred value.
Maximum folio size supported is one page shifted by the pagecache maximum when transparent huge pages are enabled and a single page otherwise.

Get flag bits occupy the low nine positions from least significant upward in accessed, lock, create, write, no-filesystem, no-wait, for-mmap, stable and dontcache order, with order carried in the top six bits starting at bit twenty-six.

Default readahead window is one hundred twenty-eight kibibytes expressed in pages, filemap migration support is absent indicated by a null handler, and the pagewalk header defines its once-only include guard.
